body:
The job that indexes real payments runs once a day. The fabricating writer it replaced ran every five minutes.

## The regression

`apps/web/vercel.json`:

```json
{ "crons": [ { "path": "/api/sync", "schedule": "0 0 * * *" } ] }
```

PR #47 ("decode real SAC transfers; unify the payments schema") records the writers it retired, including:

| Writer | Cadence |
|---|---|
| `sync_github.js` | cron every 5 min |

So the same change that made the indexed data real also slowed indexing by roughly 288x. That looks like a consequence of the Vercel Hobby plan's daily cron limit rather than a deliberate choice — nothing in #47 discusses cadence.

## Why it matters

**The dashboard contradicts itself.** It polls for live data every 15 seconds against a table that is updated once a day. A merchant who takes a payment sees nothing until the next midnight run, with no indication the view is stale.

**It erodes the safety margin against RPC retention.** `MAX_LOOKBACK` in `route.ts:37` is 100,000 ledgers, roughly 5.8 days at ~5s per ledger. Beyond that window, events are gone from Soroban RPC and unrecoverable. At a daily cadence that is about five consecutive failures before permanent data loss; at five minutes it would be over 1,600.

**Failures are invisible.** There is no alerting on the cron, so a run that 500s is indistinguishable from a day with no payments — for up to 24 hours, against a ~6 day loss horizon.

## Suggested fix

1. Move the schedule to a few minutes (`*/5 * * * *` restores parity). This requires Vercel Pro — Hobby permits only daily crons — so it is a billing decision as much as a code one.
2. Add alerting on a non-200 from `/api/sync`, or surface `sync_state.updated_at` somewhere visible.
3. Consider showing last-synced time in the dashboard so staleness is legible rather than silent.

If staying on Hobby is preferred, an external scheduler (GitHub Actions cron, or any uptime pinger) can call `/api/sync` on a tighter interval — the endpoint is already protected by `CRON_SECRET` (`route.ts:59-65`), so it is safe to drive externally.

Related: #62 (pagination) — a tighter cadence also reduces the chance of exceeding the per-run event cap.

Found while assessing whether the removed Go indexer was worth restoring.

comments.body:
**Correction — the central claim in this issue is wrong.** I filed it after reading `apps/web/vercel.json` without checking `.github/workflows/`, and the daily Vercel cron is not the real schedule.

`f3dcd65` ("fix(cron): daily Vercel cron; trigger real cadence from Actions", 2026-07-22) landed the same day as #47 and set this up deliberately. `.github/workflows/sync.yml` calls `/api/sync` on `*/5 * * * *`, authenticated with `CRON_SECRET`, and its header comment says explicitly that the Vercel daily cron is a **backstop**. Both `SYNC_URL` and `CRON_SECRET` are set as repository secrets, and recent runs are succeeding.

So there was no 288x regression, and the cadence was never left at daily by accident. Apologies for the noise.

## What is actually true

The `*/5` schedule is not being honoured. Actual start times of the last 12 runs:

```
2026-08-04T10:07:02Z   2026-08-03T23:42:13Z   2026-08-03T18:11:12Z
2026-08-04T07:20:11Z   2026-08-03T22:30:26Z   2026-08-03T16:11:50Z
2026-08-04T04:32:16Z   2026-08-03T21:17:00Z   2026-08-03T13:46:45Z
2026-08-04T01:09:20Z   2026-08-03T20:00:42Z   2026-08-03T10:59:04Z
```

Intervals range from ~1h13m to ~3h23m. Nothing close to five minutes. GitHub deprioritises and drops high-frequency scheduled workflows on shared runners, and a `*/5` cron is firing roughly every 1-3 hours in practice.

That is better than daily, so the severity here is much lower than originally written. But the gap between the configured schedule and the real one is worth knowing about, because it is invisible unless you look at run history.

## Revised scope

1. **Staleness is not surfaced.** The dashboard polls every 15s against data that can be up to three hours old, with nothing indicating that. `sync_state.updated_at` already exists and would make this legible.
2. **Partial syncs pass silently.** Since #64, `/api/sync` returns `drained: false` when paging stops against its time budget. The workflow only checks the HTTP code and `"success":false`, so a run that indexed part of a backlog is reported as a clean success.
3. **If sub-hour freshness is actually required**, GitHub Actions cannot deliver it. That is a Vercel Pro decision, not something to fix in this repo.

Retitling and rescoping accordingly. Item 2 is small and concrete; I will take that one now.

Assigning to @wagmiiii alongside #36 and #28, since all three sit on the indexer's data plane.

Two corrections before anyone picks this up — the issue is half right, and the wrong half will send someone down a dead end.

**The 288x claim is wrong.** `vercel.json` is daily because Vercel's Hobby plan makes more than one cron per day a hard deploy failure, but that is not the real cadence. `.github/workflows/sync.yml` triggers `/api/sync` on a 5-minute schedule; GitHub throttles high-frequency workflows, so it lands every one to three hours in practice. Recent runs bear that out. So the gap versus the writer it replaced is roughly 12-36x, not 288x, and the `MAX_LOOKBACK` safety-margin arithmetic in the issue body should be redone against that.

**The invisibility half was real and is now fixed.** `apps/web/src/lib/sync-status.ts` (landed 2026-08-05, 17 tests) classifies indexed data as live / lagging / stale / unknown and both `/dashboard` and `/api/payments` consume it, so a merchant is now told when the number on screen is old instead of being shown a stale total as if it were current. Its thresholds are set from the observed one-to-three-hour cadence rather than the configured schedule, deliberately, so a normal gap is not reported as a fault.

**What is genuinely left:** deciding whether one-to-three hours is acceptable for the product, and if not, moving the trigger somewhere without the throttle. That is a smaller and different question than the one this issue was opened with, so the title and body are worth rewriting before work starts rather than closing and reopening.

title: fix(ci): sync staleness and partial syncs are invisible

## Summary
Rescoped. The Go poller's concurrent ledger processing described here no longer exists — `/api/sync` processes a range single-threaded per invocation.

The race is narrower now but still real: an overlapping manual trigger and scheduled cron run can both call `setLastSyncedLedger`, letting an older ledger overwrite a newer one and causing duplicate processing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Make the cursor update atomic and conditional (`UPDATE ... SET last_ledger = $1 WHERE last_ledger < $1`).
- [ ] Consider a Postgres advisory lock so overlapping invocations do not double-process a range.
- [ ] Test demonstrating that an older write cannot clobber a newer cursor.

## Tech Stack
TypeScript, `pg`, PostgreSQL, Vitest


## Important
Please make sure to read our [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/accensa/accensa-app/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before you start working on this issue.

comments.body:
Assigning to @wagmiiii with #63, #28, and #11.

Worth flagging that this got more urgent since it was rescoped on 2026-08-03. The rescope noted the race needed "an overlapping manual trigger and scheduled cron run" — at the time there was no manual trigger, so the window was mostly theoretical. PR #70 (2026-08-04) added a "Sync now" button to the dashboard, so a merchant can now produce exactly that overlap by clicking during a scheduled run.

The unguarded write is still there, at `apps/web/src/lib/db.ts:182`:

```sql
INSERT INTO sync_state (id, last_ledger, updated_at) VALUES (1, $1, now())
ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET last_ledger = EXCLUDED.last_ledger, updated_at = now()
```

Unconditional — an older ledger will happily overwrite a newer one, which is the first acceptance criterion in the issue body.

One interaction to be aware of while fixing it: `event-pager.ts` (2026-08-05) made `/api/sync` refuse to advance the cursor past a ledger it only partially drained. That is a correctness guard on the *value* being written, not on the ordering of concurrent writes, so it does not overlap with the fix here — but the conditional `WHERE last_ledger < $1` needs to compose with it rather than replace it. The manual trigger is rate-limited (see `sync-status.ts`), which narrows the window but does not close it.

body:
## Summary
Rescoped for the serverless architecture (the long-running Go poller was removed in #49).

`/api/sync` now runs as a scheduled invocation. A transient Soroban RPC failure fails the whole run and the cursor does not advance, so the range is retried on the next schedule. That is safe, but coarse: a single event that always fails to decode blocks indexing progress indefinitely.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Exponential backoff for Soroban RPC calls within a run (up to 3 attempts).
- [ ] `dead_letter_events` table for events that repeatedly fail to process.
- [ ] Allow the cursor to advance past a dead-lettered event, so one bad event cannot stall the indexer.
- [ ] Vitest coverage for the retry path and dead-letter insertion.

## Tech Stack
TypeScript, Next.js App Router route handlers, `pg`, PostgreSQL, Vitest


## Important
Please make sure to read our [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/accensa/accensa-app/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before you start working on this issue.
title: feat(indexer): implement retry mechanism and dead-letter queue for failed RPC requests
